A.rationale: The histopathological examination reveals a classic-appearing hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts and proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells, which is consistent with squamous cell carcinoma, clear cell variant.

B.rationale: The histopathological examination does not support seborrheic keratosis as the most likely diagnosis.

C.rationale: The histopathological examination reveals invasive features, which is not consistent with Bowen's disease (squamous cell carcinoma in situ).

D.rationale: The histopathological examination reveals a hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts and proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells, which is consistent with invasive squamous cell carcinoma arising in a seborrheic keratosis of the eyelid.

vignette_preview:
A man in his mid-80s presented with a 4-year history of a left lower eyelid mass, noted by his wife to have recently grown and acquired a crust.

On examination, a yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule was discovered on the central lower eyelid without margin involvement. At one lateral end, the tumor had acquired a flakier surface.
